title: Studio measures only from telemetry, in the organisation's Loki

statements.says: Studio no longer reads Transcripts.
Everything Studio shows comes from Claude Code's OpenTelemetry events in Loki.
Studio keeps no database of its own.
Loki's address is configuration, and the AppHost's Collector and Loki stand in for the organisation's until real resources exist.
Studio gives up showing the branch.
Studio gives up thinking tokens and the split of cache writes into 5-minute and 1-hour.
Studio gives up showing a skill's arguments.
Studio gives up per-skill spend for a plugin from a private marketplace, the catalogue included.
Studio gives up reporting faults and local history.
Spend that Claude Code does not name is shown as its own amount.
Totals come from LogQL aggregate queries.
A Filter span longer than Loki's query limit is split into several queries.
An Activation shows only what skill_activated says, and Studio never joins events to fill in a field an event does not carry.
Tests run against a real Loki in a container.
In an organisation every developer has their own machine, so a Transcript on one laptop tells Studio nothing about the rest.
Only what reaches a central store can be measured.
The events carry almost everything the Transcripts did.
skill_activated names the skill, its trigger, source, plugin and marketplace once OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1 is set.
api_request carries one request's model, effort, tokens by kind, request_id, cost_usd and the skill in force.
From Claude Code 2.1.269, OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_REPOSITORY=true puts vcs.* repository attributes on every event.
No skill or request event carries the branch.
Telemetry reports neither thinking tokens nor the 5-minute and 1-hour cache write split.
Arguments are only in a tool_result or, for a typed skill, in prompt text that is redacted unless every developer's prompts are sent to the store.
skill.name on api_request is the literal third-party for a plugin from a private marketplace, and no setting lifts it.
Nothing reports a lost event, and nothing sent before telemetry was switched on is ever seen.
Because totals come from aggregate queries, a busy organisation never cuts them short, and only a list of individual events can hit the read cap.
Tests run against a real Loki because the queries are where the logic now lives.

Pricing each Turn with Studio's own Price table was rejected, because an organisation sets its contracted prices once through the modelPricing managed setting, and a Studio table would be one developer's opinion of the price.
The Price table was also turned down because telemetry lacks the token kinds it priced and spells the model differently, and the table was the last thing in SQLite.

Crediting third-party spend to the latest plugin skill activated in the same session was rejected, because nested skills and parallel subagents can each have a different plugin skill in force, nothing in the event says which, and with the Transcripts gone nothing could check the guess.

Prometheus for spend was rejected, because the cost and token metrics carry the same redaction as the events, with no request or prompt id, as 60-second deltas, and Loki's aggregate queries give the same totals.
This record supersedes the earlier record that gave telemetry two stores, SQLite for transcripts and Loki for events.
